<Phase type="activation">

Picture a gym membership billed every month. Whether you go or not, the charge arrives on the same day.

**An installment to the venue is the same kind of membership.** Think about what you will pay it with in a month when nobody bought a place.

</Phase>

<Phase type="reflection">

Go back to the membership. It is paid from a salary, not from hope for next month.

**A monthly venue payment is paid with places sold.** If places do not sell, you pay it.

</Phase>

<Phase type="concept">

## The pace of sales against the payment schedule

Venues that offer installments tell leaders this calculation. The monthly payment is 2–3 thousand dollars, a place costs 4 thousand. Then one or two places sold a month cover the payment. That holds if the guest pays the whole price at once.

If the guest pays only the first part, you need more sales. In the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) the monthly venue payment is 6,750 dollars, and a guest's first payment is 900. To cover a month with first payments alone, you need seven or eight new guests.

## What the calculator shows

In the teaching deal sales run evenly, and the gap is 17,028 dollars in the third month. Try a different pace:

- sales in the last two months — the gap grows to 29,250;
- the guest pays everything at once — no gap;
- a 50 % first payment and early sales together — a gap of 150 dollars.

**The pace of sales is a plan line just like the price.** It has to be set in advance, not hoped for.

## The venue is booked after the minimum

Experienced leaders do not sign with the venue until first payments from the minimum group are in. The minimum is your break-even from the calculator. Then the first venue payment is paid by guests.

## Payment options for the guest

Different guests prefer different things. Offer a few paths:

- **paying in full** — a few percent off the price or a small bonus, such as a one-to-one meeting;
- **an early price** — the first payment locks in a lower price than closer to arrival;
- **three payments** — on the dates when you pay the venue.

Write the terms of each option and the refund dates in advance, using the scale from module 02.

<SelfCheck id="c3"/>

</Phase>

<Phase type="practice">

1. Open the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) and find the sales curve.
2. Switch it to "late", then to "early". Write down the gap in both cases.
3. Set the guest's first payment to 50 % and choose early sales. See what is left of the gap.
4. For your retreat, write a sales plan: how many places in each month before arrival.
5. Mark the month in which you have the minimum group. That is the earliest date to sign with the venue.

</Phase>
